title: Path Aliases
definition: A feature configured in `tsconfig.json` that allows you to define custom module resolution paths. It replaces long, messy relative paths (`../../../components/Button`) with clean, absolute aliases (`@/components/Button`).
simpleExplanation: Imagine you are deep in a basement room of a giant house. To get to the attic, you have to go up stairs, up stairs, up stairs (`../../../`). Path Aliases are a magical teleporter. You just say `@/attic`, and you instantly import the file, no matter how deep in the basement you are.
realWorldExample: Standardizing imports in a Next.js application so that every component import starts cleanly with `@/components/...`.
useCases: Refactoring (moving a file doesn't break its relative imports)

basic: What two properties in `tsconfig` are required to setup path aliases?
intermediate: Does TypeScript actually change the paths in the compiled JavaScript output?
advanced: Why do path aliases often fail at runtime in Node.js apps?

answers.question: What two properties are required?
answers.answer: You MUST set `"baseUrl"` (usually to `"."` or `"./src"`), and then configure the `"paths"` mapping object.

answers.question: Why do they fail at runtime in Node.js?
answers.answer: TypeScript ONLY uses Path Aliases to resolve Types during compilation. It DOES NOT rewrite the paths in the generated `.js` files! Node.js will crash saying 'Cannot find module @/components'. You must use a tool like `tsc-alias`, `tsconfig-paths`, or a bundler (Webpack/Vite) to physically rewrite the paths for runtime.
